raw_response:
I have been farming these 60 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I know every piece of this land. My husband and my children sometimes work off-farm in the city, so I cannot manage too much labor-heavy cotton. Wheat and maize are my backbone — they give us grain to eat and sell, and the machines can do most of the work now. I will put 45 mu into my wheat-maize rotation and keep 15 mu for cotton. That is enough cotton to bring in cash, but not so much that I break my back picking it at my age.

For wheat, I will rotary till the land before sowing in October, like everyone else here. I will sow an improved variety from the seed shop — the yield is steady and the grain buyer recognizes it. I will put down compound fertilizer as a base and topdress urea in spring when the wheat turns green. Water is precious even though I have a well, so I will irrigate four times: once before winter to protect the seedlings, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I will spray herbicide early and watch for aphids and rust — about four sprays in total. I expect around 1000 jin per mu if the weather behaves.

For maize, there is no time to plough after harvesting wheat in June. I will direct-seed hybrid maize into the wheat stubble — no-tillage, using the machine service. I will apply starter fertilizer with the seed and topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage. Maize does not need as much water as wheat; I will irrigate twice, at jointing and filling, unless the summer rain is generous. Three pesticide sprays should do — herbicide at sowing and one or two insecticide sprays for corn borers. With good sun, I expect about 1100 jin per mu.

For cotton, I will rotary till in spring and plant hybrid Bt cotton seed. Cotton is thirsty when it flowers and sets bolls, so I will irrigate twice during those key periods. But the real trouble is pests — aphids, mites, and whatever else shows up — so I will spray about ten times through the season. I will use compound fertilizer at planting and add urea later. I hope for about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu. If the price drops, I might regret planting even this much, but 15 mu is manageable for us.
